question_text: What is vapour pressure? How is it related to the boiling point?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by the
vapour of a liquid when the vapour is in
equilibrium with the liquid at a given
It increases as the temperature increases.
steps.why: In a closed vessel, evaporation and condensation reach a balance; the pressure of the vapour at that balance is the liquid's vapour pressure, and higher temperature shifts the balance toward more vapour.
common_mistakes: Leaving out in equilibrium with the liquid — pressure of any vapour is not vapour pressure.
Saying it depends on the amount of liquid. It depends on the liquid's nature and temperature only.
steps.memory_tip: Closed vessel, balance reached, vapour's pressure read — that reading is the vapour pressure.
steps.margin_note: Equilibrium and at a given temperature are the marked phrases.

steps.label: The boiling-point relation

lines.text: A liquid boils when its vapour pressure equals the external pressure

lines: The boiling point is the temperature at which
lowers the boiling point; higher pressure
steps.why: Boiling is bubble formation inside the liquid, and a bubble can only survive when the vapour pushing it open matches the outside pressure pressing it shut. That equality defines the boiling point.
common_mistakes: Giving 100 °C as the definition of boiling point. 100 °C is water's boiling point only at 1 atm.
Saying the vapour pressure must EXCEED the external pressure. Boiling starts when the two are equal.
steps.memory_tip: Boiling happens when the vapour pressure reaches the outside pressure.
steps.margin_note: Name both examples: hills for lower outside pressure, pressure cooker for higher. They are the same rule read in two directions.

insider_note: Two questions, one mark each, and the second is a single sentence about two pressures being equal. Give the definition, then the relation; there is nothing else at two marks worth the space.
